sections.title: Sources and Methodology
sections.narrative: Pipeline: news ingestion → event detection → entity normalisation → article claims (passages verified verbatim) + knowledge-base relationships → scored graph → ranked paths → market windows from the configured provider → explanation validated against the evidence package.

window_definitions.anchor_date: The event's information time (earliest source-article timestamp, else the event date), converted to the asset's exchange time zone, taken as a calendar date.
window_definitions.reference_close: The last available close on a trading day strictly before the anchor date (pre-event baseline). Intraday timing is unknown, so a window may include same-day moves that happened before the news.
window_definitions.window_k: The close of the k-th trading session on or after the anchor date (session 1 = the anchor date if it is a trading day). Trading days are the dates present in the provider's series, so each market's weekends and holidays are skipped.
window_definitions.return_pct: (close at window k / reference close - 1) x 100, in the asset's quote currency; no FX conversion. For yield instruments the value is the change in the yield level.
window_definitions.window_status: AVAILABLE = computed; NOT_YET_ELAPSED = the k-th session has not happened yet; MISSING = the session should exist but the provider has no observation.
window_definitions.historical_comparison: For comparable past events: the 5-trading-day return using the same definitions, compared with the direction implied by the impact path. Co-movement is context, not proof of causation.
